title: Bob's input set of the mixed sample
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$ and consider two samples $\omega_X$ and $\omega_Y$ drawn from the hard-distribution sample space on the coordinates $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$. Suppose the two samples share the same special coordinate $T$, that they agree on Alice's input bits before the special coordinate, and that they agree on Bob's input bits after the special coordinate. Then Bob's input set of the mixed sample $\operatorname{mix}(\omega_X,\omega_Y)$ — the sample that takes Alice's data from $\omega_X$ and Bob's data from $\omega_Y$ — coincides with Bob's input set of $\omega_Y$.
hypotheses_covered: the two samples have the same special coordinate T
Alice's bits before the special coordinate agree
Bob's bits after the special coordinate agree
replaced: The mixed sample has Bob's full input from the second sample.
